subject: physics
title: Atomic, Nuclear & Particle Physics Adventure 1: Rutherford scattering and atomic spectra
welcome_lead: Today you'll fire alpha particles at gold foil with Rutherford.
meta_desc: Physics — Rutherford-Geiger-Marsden experiment, energy levels, hf = E₂ - E₁.
final_note: You learned alpha scattering revealed a small dense + nucleus; emission spectra come from electrons falling between discrete energy levels: hf = E₂ - E₁.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Thomson's plum pudding (1904): positive mush with electrons in it.

Geiger and Marsden (1909) directed α at gold foil — most went through, but ~1 in 8000 was scattered back!

Rutherford (1911): only a tiny dense + nucleus could deflect α like that. Most of the atom is empty space.

Bohr (1913): electrons orbit in discrete energy levels, only certain orbits allowed.

Electron falls from E₂ to E₁ → emits photon: hf = E₂ − E₁.

h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s (Planck constant).

Hydrogen Balmer series: visible emission lines from n ≥ 3 falling to n = 2.

Emission: hot gas radiates discrete lines.

Absorption: cool gas in front of hot source — dark lines at same wavelengths.

Fraunhofer lines in sun's spectrum identified He (1868) before Earth observation.

Today: helps identify composition of distant stars + galaxies — cornerstone of astrophysics.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between brittle and ductile materials?
options: Brittle materials are weak and ductile materials are strong.
The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.
Brittle materials fracture with little or no plastic deformation; ductile materials undergo significant plastic deformation before breaking.
Brittle materials are metals and ductile materials are non-metals.

mcqs.q: What determines the de Broglie wavelength of a particle?
options: Its momentum (lambda = h/p) — heavier or faster particles have shorter de Broglie wavelengths.
Its kinetic energy alone, with no dependence on mass.
Brittle materials are metals and ductile materials are non-metals.

mcqs.q: How do you see a non-luminous object like a book?
options: Brittle materials are metals and ductile materials are non-metals.
Your eyes send out beams of vision that hit the book and let you see it.
Light from a source reflects off the book and enters your eyes.
The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.
